trust_boundaries: developer-to-scm: developer code push to github_repo
architecture_summary.operational_context: Cloud CI/CD pipeline for software delivery with production deployment

threat_actors.name: Malicious Contributor
threat_actors.motivation: Supply chain compromise — inject malicious code into production
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Developer account takeover or malicious PR submission
non_capabilities: No direct access to production infrastructure
No access to secrets_manager without CI pipeline execution
No ability to modify branch protection rules without admin privileges

threat_actors.name: External Supply Chain Attacker
threat_actors.motivation: Inject malware into software artifacts for downstream victims
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Compromise of GitHub Actions runner or dependency poisoning
non_capabilities: No physical access to runner infrastructure
No access to Artifactory admin interface without CI credentials

attack_paths.entry_point: Malicious GitHub Actions workflow file committed to repository
attack_paths.impact: Arbitrary code execution on CI runner with access to all secrets
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: GitHub Actions workflow injection is well-documented; requires branch protection bypass or PR approval

attack_paths.entry_point: Environment variables or build logs exposing secrets during AP-001 execution
attack_paths.impact: Production credentials exfiltrated enabling direct prod_env access
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Secrets leakage in CI logs is extremely common; debug logging frequently exposes env vars

attack_paths.entry_point: Malicious artifact published by compromised runner (AP-001)
attack_paths.impact: Backdoored software artifact propagated to all downstream deployments
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Artifact signing not confirmed; malicious artifacts would be deployed without signature verification

attack_paths.impact: Direct access to production environment bypassing staging gate
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires AP-002 success; deploy keys may be scoped to prevent direct use outside pipeline

attack_paths.entry_point: Workflow modification to skip or suppress SAST scan results
attack_paths.impact: Malicious code bypasses security scanning gate before artifact publication
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: SAST bypass is common in pipelines without enforced quality gates; workflow modification is trivial with repo write access

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised GitHub account used to modify branch protection rules
attack_paths.impact: Removal of code review requirements, enabling single-actor code injection
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires GitHub admin-level compromise; high value but harder to achieve without targeted attack

mitigations.control_name: Pin GitHub Actions to commit SHA; require PR review
Secrets management with masked outputs and no-log directives
Artifact signing with Sigstore/cosign and signature verification at deploy
Deploy key rotation and scoped permissions
Required SAST gate with enforcement — non-bypassable step
MFA and privileged access management for repository admins

findings.severity_rationale: Secrets leakage from CI logs gives attacker production credentials; impact extends beyond CI to all systems the credentials access
Unsigned artifact in Artifactory can be replaced or backdoored; every downstream deployment inherits the compromise
Runner workflow injection enables arbitrary code execution in CI with full secrets access
SAST gate bypass allows malicious code to pass security screening undetected
Branch protection manipulation requires admin compromise which is separately mitigated; residual risk is low with MFA enforced
